stem: Which one of the following is a landlocked country?

stem: Which of the following is not a capital city of a country?
expl: Sydney is not the capital of any country. Canberra is the capital of Australia, Wellington is the capital of New Zealand, and Riyadh is the capital of Saudi Arabia.

stem: name the city of russia that is known as ‘venice of the north’.

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: Saint Petersburg is called the “Venice of the North”. Earlier, it was known as Petrograd and Leningrad. It is an important historical and cultural city and also a port city.

stem: Which of the following is known as ‘Mistress of the eastern Sea’?
expl: “Mistress of the Eastern Seas” is a title given to India. In some references, this title has also been used for Sri Lanka.

stem: Which of the following is the playground of europe?
expl: Switzerland is called the Playground of Europe due to its natural beauty, outdoor sports, and tourism activities.

stem: The surface of the earth covered with water is approximately?
expl: Approximately two-thirds of the Earth’s surface is covered by water.

stem: A ridge of 64000 km. length and 2000 km to 2400 km width passing through the north and south Atlantic oceanic basin enters into the south Pacific oceanic basin through the indian oceanic basin and then from the middle of Australia and Antarctic. This ridge is –
expl: The above characteristics are related to the Mid-Ocean Ridge. The Mid-Ocean Ridge extends around the globe for about 40,390 miles or nearly 65,000 km, spreading through the Arctic, Atlantic, Indian and Pacific Oceans. It is the largest geological feature on the Earth’s surface.
The Ninety East Ridge (90° East Ridge) is a ridge located in the Indian Ocean.

stem: Where does the El Niño current flow?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: El Niño is a naturally occurring climate pattern associated with a rise in sea-surface temperatures in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean. It affects the Indian monsoon rainfall and can create drought-like conditions. Thus, El Niño and the Southern Oscillation are associated with weak and deficient monsoon rainfall in the Indian subcontinent. La Niña indicates lower temperatures in the equatorial eastern Pacific Ocean, which is opposite to El Niño.
